clue.text: Watch revues call in comic

indicators.note: comic means funny or ridiculous, so the letters of these three words are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: An invitation to watch a theatre's comic revues being phoned in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comic' looks like a description of the revues but it signals the rearrangement of REVUESCALLIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping a close watch on someone is the business of monitoring or observation.

clue.text: Maybe some bread roll found inside case

indicators.note: found inside places one word within the other

parts.note: a suit is a lawsuit, a case in court
a bun is a bread roll

explanation.surface: A sandwich roll discovered in someone's luggage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' looks like luggage but is a legal case. The definition 'Maybe some' means part of a whole, by example.
explanation.definitionFit: A component forming part of a larger whole is a portion, so 'some' of it, perhaps.

clue.text: Run over from Beetle car, terribly upset

indicators.note: upset says the hidden letters are read backwards
from says the letters are taken out of the words that follow it

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A VW Beetle driven so badly that it knocks someone down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' signals the letters lie within the words; 'upset' turns them round in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To go back over a route or argument again is to repeat it.

clue.text: Boss of former unit on hospital department

parts.note: ex means former
a cell is a small unit, as in an organisation
ENT, ear nose and throat, is a hospital department

explanation.surface: A boss who used to run a unit sitting above a hospital department.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boss' looks like a manager but is slang for first-rate.
explanation.definitionFit: Boss is informal, especially in Liverpool, for superb or first-rate.

clue.text: Area in Scottish lake for fish

indicators.note: in places the area letter inside the lake

parts.note: a loch is a Scottish lake

explanation.surface: A part of a Scottish loch good for fishing.
explanation.definitionFit: A small freshwater species with barbels around its mouth.

clue.text: Heard I'm in favour of a jar

indicators.note: heard means the phrase is said aloud

parts.note: I'm is I am, so am; pro means in favour of; the indefinite article, A

explanation.surface: Someone overheard backing a particular jar.
explanation.definitionFit: An ancient Greek or Roman two-handled vessel for wine or oil.

clue.text: After tea I knock up Indian speciality

indicators.note: after places the tea first, the rest following it

parts.note: cha is slang for tea

indicators.note: up in a down clue says the letters are read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: to tap is to knock

explanation.surface: A cook knocks up an Indian dish after a cup of tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knock up' looks like a phrasal verb for cooking, but 'up' reverses I TAP.
explanation.definitionFit: An unleavened flatbread from the subcontinent, a staple of the cuisine.

clue.text: Trained person if also rubbish

indicators.note: rubbish means poor or useless, so the letters are reworked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A qualified expert who is nevertheless no good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trained person' looks like the definition, but 'person' is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone qualified by formal training for a career works to that standard.

clue.text: Automatic rifle beginning to oddly jerk

parts.note: to rifle is to ransack or rob

indicators.note: the beginning of the word oddly means only its opening letter is used

parts.note: a tic is an involuntary jerk of a muscle

explanation.surface: An automatic rifle that starts to jerk strangely when fired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rifle' looks like the gun but is the verb meaning to ransack.
explanation.definitionFit: Something mechanical and unthinking, acting like a machine, is described as automatic.

clue.text: Praise a god, say, keeping very quiet

indicators.note: keeping means holding something inside, so the quiet letters sit within the other pieces
say signals that the word for a god is taken by how it is pronounced

parts.note: the Lord is God; in a non-rhotic British accent the word is pronounced like laud
pp, pianissimo, is the musical marking for very quiet

explanation.surface: An instruction to worship a deity, but softly.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent, which drops the R, 'Lord' is pronounced just like 'laud'.
explanation.definitionFit: To applaud someone is to commend or express approval of them, a verb of approval.

clue.text: Argument made steering awkward

indicators.note: awkward means clumsy, so these letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A row caused by difficult steering of a car.
explanation.definitionFit: A quarrel or dispute is a falling-out of opinions.

clue.text: Pigeon let down catching insect

indicators.note: catching means holding something within, so one word sits inside the other

parts.note: to fail someone is to let them down
an ant is an insect

explanation.surface: A pigeon disappoints its keeper by snapping up a bug.
explanation.definitionFit: A breed of domestic dove with a fanned-out spread of tail feathers.

clue.text: Cheers seeing house with old beams

parts.note: rays are beams of light

explanation.surface: Applause greets the sight of an old timbered house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beams' suggests timber but means rays of light.
explanation.definitionFit: Shouts of hurrah are cheers of celebration or approval.

clue.text: Composer saw audience thrilled in Eroica initially

indicators.note: initially means the opening letter of each of the five words is taken

explanation.surface: A composer watched a crowd enraptured by Beethoven's Eroica symphony.
explanation.walkthrough: The Eroica is a Beethoven symphony, a fitting distraction for a composer clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Erik Satie was a French composer, famous for the Gymnopédies piano pieces.

clue.text: Conclude EastEnders' trial, winning

parts.note: to end is to conclude

indicators.note: East Enders are Cockneys, who famously drop their aitches, so the opening H goes

parts.note: a hearing is a trial in court

explanation.surface: A soap opera wraps up a courtroom storyline on a high.
explanation.walkthrough: EastEnders is a long-running BBC soap set in London's East End; here it means Cockney speakers, who say 'earing for HEARING.
explanation.definitionFit: A winning smile or manner is charming and lovable, an adjective of appeal.

clue.text: Preparing fish, empty sac during handling

indicators.note: during places the letters inside the other word

parts.note: dealing with something is handling it

indicators.note: empty means the inner letter of sac is removed, leaving its outsides

explanation.surface: Gutting a fish, a cook empties a sac in the process.
explanation.definitionFit: Removing the scales from fish is a step in getting it ready for cooking.

clue.text: Swamps single sister with boyfriends?

parts.note: I, the Roman numeral one, means single
a nun is a religious sister
dates are romantic partners; the question mark says boyfriends are only one example

explanation.surface: A single woman's sister overwhelms her with suitors.
explanation.definitionFit: To swamp is to flood or overwhelm, as water does land.

clue.text: Dirty European occupying a French house

parts.note: un is French for a

indicators.note: occupying means sitting inside something else

parts.note: a house is a family line, a clan

explanation.surface: A grubby European living in a French home.
explanation.definitionFit: Something soiled and grimy lacks cleanliness, the opposite of spotless.

clue.text: Notwithstanding abnormal speed, embraces sex

indicators.note: embraces means holding something inside
abnormal means not in its usual form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: it is a common euphemism for sex or sex appeal

explanation.surface: Despite excessive speed, someone indulges in sex.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abnormal' rearranges speed to DESPE. 'It' as a euphemism for sex is a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are prepositions meaning in spite of, regardless of.

clue.text: Oddly plump cases transforming insects

indicators.note: oddly means the first, third, fifth and further odd-numbered letters are taken from the words plump cases

explanation.surface: Fat chrysalises containing insects mid-metamorphosis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cases' looks like the cocoon of the surface but is only fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the chrysalis stage in which larvae metamorphose into adult forms.

clue.text: Equality over top of nude model

parts.note: par means equality, as in on a par
ago means over, past

indicators.note: top of in a down clue means the first letter of nude

explanation.surface: An equal-rights call topping a nude model.
explanation.walkthrough: 'model' looks like an artist's sitter but means a perfect example.
explanation.definitionFit: A perfect example to be imitated, a model of virtue, for instance.

clue.text: Boozer on board tramp ship

indicators.note: on board means inside, like cargo in the vessel

parts.note: to tramp is to walk, pace
a boozer is British slang for a pub, an inn

explanation.surface: A drunk taken aboard a tramp steamer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tramp' looks like a tramp ship, but it means to walk heavily.
explanation.definitionFit: A small boat carried by a larger vessel, a type of tender.

clue.text: Split, a capital city?

parts.note: Split is a Croatian city, not a capital; read instead as a capital that is split, divided between Greek and Turkish Cypriot sides

explanation.surface: A geography quiz question asking whether Split is a capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Split looks like the Croatian port; the clue means a divided capital.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital of Cyprus has been partitioned by a buffer zone since 1974.

clue.text: A new hair product for sweetheart

parts.note: gel is a hair styling product

explanation.surface: A new styling gel bought as a gift for a lover.
explanation.definitionFit: A term of endearment for a loved one, a darling.

clue.text: NATO is one friend in a million

indicators.note: in places the friend inside the other letters

parts.note: a crony is a close friend

explanation.surface: The military alliance described as a friend in a million.
explanation.definitionFit: The alliance's name is formed from initials, North Atlantic Treaty Organization.

clue.text: Ogling the French sweetheart with girdle

parts.note: le is French for the
the heart of the word sweet is its central letter E
a ring encircles, as a girdle does

explanation.surface: A Frenchman eyeing up his girlfriend in her corset.
explanation.definitionFit: Leering means looking at someone lasciviously, staring with unpleasant desire.

clue.text: Flipping raining around drive home

indicators.note: around means present within, so the letters sit inside the words flipping raining

explanation.surface: Annoyed at the rain while driving home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' looks like a mild British oath or an anagram signal, but it is just part of the text concealing the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To drive home an idea is to fix it firmly in the mind, to instil it.

clue.text: Dope perhaps seeing reason

definitions.meaning: dope is slang for information or inside knowledge, the kind spies gather
reason here is the faculty of the mind, intellect

explanation.surface: Drugs perhaps lead to sound judgement.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both gathered secret information and the mental capacity to understand.
